top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards one identifiable, reproduced invention, the optical lattice clock based on magic-wavelength trapping, which carried frequency measurement to the 10^-18 level and has concrete consequences in geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and dark-matter searches. The two-name allocation to Katori and Ye is the cleanest on the slate, and a citation anchored on magic-wavelength trapping keeps it distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. P002 is mature and conceptually broader, but the HgTe route traces to Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who are outside the three names, so the credit is incomplete and hard to defend in a citation. I still prefer P002 to no award because both proposals are sound science.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; documented connections (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+, XL-Calibur) involve none of Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp
